def git(repo, *args, strip=True):
    out = subprocess.run(GIT + list(args), cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return out.strip() if strip else out.rstrip(chr(10))


def changed_since(repo, base):
    committed = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", f"{base}..HEAD").splitlines())
    working = set(git(repo, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", strip=False).splitlines())
    working = {line[3:] for line in working}
    return committed | working


def scope_check(repo, base, budget):
    files = sorted(changed_since(repo, base))
    return ("fail" if len(files) > budget else "pass"), len(files)


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def cache_valid(cache, manifest, now, ttl, runtime):
    if not cache:
        return False, "no cache"
    if now - cache["checked_at"] > ttl:
        return False, "expired"
    if cache["manifest_sha"] != sha(manifest):
        return False, "manifest changed"
    if cache["runtime"] != runtime:
        return False, "runtime changed"
    return True, "fresh and inputs unchanged""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"in_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() builds a temporary git repository and measures the change budget before and after committing, tests the cache against age, manifest and runtime changes, runs a launcher through two initializers and compares repository hashes around two read-only runs.","descKn":"main() ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ git repository ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ commit ಮಾಡುವ ಮುನ್ನ ಮತ್ತು ನಂತರ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಬಜೆಟ್ ಅಳೆದು, ಕ್ಯಾಶ್ ಅನ್ನು ವಯಸ್ಸು, manifest ಮತ್ತು runtime ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು initializers ಮೂಲಕ ಲಾಂಚರ್ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಎರಡು ಓದಲು-ಮಾತ್ರ ಓಟಗಳ ಸುತ್ತ repository hash ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def section(t):

def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        repo = Path(d) / "repo"
        repo.mkdir()
        git(repo, "init", "-q")
        (repo / "src").mkdir()
        (repo / "src" / "app.py").write_text("v1\n", encoding="utf-8")
        git(repo, "add", "-A"); git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "baseline")
        base = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")

        section("1. Genuinely running: change budget against the last-known-good commit (real git)")
        print("clean tree:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        (repo / "src" / "app.py").write_text("v2\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print("one modified file:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        for i in range(4):
            (repo / f"new{i}.txt").write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
        print("one modified plus four untracked files, budget 3:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        print("changed paths:", sorted(changed_since(repo, base)))
        print("the budget counted untracked files as well; it is a coarse scope control, a single sensitive file can matter more than fifty documents, and exceeding it means a human decides, not that the baseline moves automatically")

        section("2. Genuinely checking: committed changes versus a clean working tree")
        git(repo, "add", "-A"); git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "agent work")
        print("git status --porcelain after committing:", repr(git(repo, "status", "--porcelain")))
        print("budget check still sees the committed changes:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        print("a clean working tree does not mean nothing changed: the agent could have committed everything, so the comparison is against the recorded baseline commit and not against the current index")

        section("3. Genuinely checking: the dependency cache and what invalidates it")
        manifest = Path(d) / "requirements.txt"
        manifest.write_text("pytest\n", encoding="utf-8")
        now = time.time()
        cache = {"checked_at": now - 3600, "manifest_sha": sha(manifest), "runtime": "3.14", "result": "pass"}
        ttl = 24 * 3600
        print("fresh cache:", cache_valid(cache, manifest, now, ttl, "3.14"))
        print("23 days later:", cache_valid(cache, manifest, now + 23 * 86400, ttl, "3.14"))
        manifest.write_text("pytest\nrequests\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print("manifest edited ten minutes after the check:", cache_valid(cache, manifest, now + 600, ttl, "3.14"))
        manifest.write_text("pytest\n", encoding="utf-8")

ಅದರ manifest hash ಹಾಗೂ runtime ಹೊಂದಬೇಕು.","code":"GIT = ["git", "-c", "user.name=lab", "-c", "user.email=lab@example.com", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false"]


def git(repo, *args, strip=True):
    out = subprocess.run(GIT + list(args), cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return out.strip() if strip else out.rstrip(chr(10))


def changed_since(repo, base):
    committed = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", f"{base}..HEAD").splitlines())
    working = set(git(repo, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", strip=False).splitlines())
    working = {line[3:] for line in working}
    return committed | working


def scope_check(repo, base, budget):
    files = sorted(changed_since(repo, base))
    return ("fail" if len(files) > budget else "pass"), len(files)


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def cache_valid(cache, manifest, now, ttl, runtime):
    if not cache:
        return False, "no cache"
    if now - cache["checked_at"] > ttl:
        return False, "expired"
    if cache["manifest_sha"] != sha(manifest):
        return False, "manifest changed"
    if cache["runtime"] != runtime:
        return False, "runtime changed"
    return True, "fresh and inputs unchanged""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"in_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() builds a temporary git repository and measures the change budget before and after committing, tests the cache against age, manifest and runtime changes, runs a launcher through two initializers and compares repository hashes around two read-only runs.","descKn":"main() ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ git repository ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ commit ಮಾಡುವ ಮುನ್ನ ಮತ್ತು ನಂತರ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಬಜೆಟ್ ಅಳೆದು, ಕ್ಯಾಶ್ ಅನ್ನು ವಯಸ್ಸು, manifest ಮತ್ತು runtime ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು initializers ಮೂಲಕ ಲಾಂಚರ್ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಎರಡು ಓದಲು-ಮಾತ್ರ ಓಟಗಳ ಸುತ್ತ repository hash ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def section(t):

        (repo / "src").mkdir()
        (repo / "src" / "app.py").write_text("v1\n", encoding="utf-8")
        git(repo, "add", "-A"); git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "baseline")
        base = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")

        section("1. Genuinely running: change budget against the last-known-good commit (real git)")
        print("clean tree:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        (repo / "src" / "app.py").write_text("v2\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print("one modified file:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        for i in range(4):
            (repo / f"new{i}.txt").write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
        print("one modified plus four untracked files, budget 3:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        print("changed paths:", sorted(changed_since(repo, base)))
        print("the budget counted untracked files as well; it is a coarse scope control, a single sensitive file can matter more than fifty documents, and exceeding it means a human decides, not that the baseline moves automatically")

        section("2. Genuinely checking: committed changes versus a clean working tree")
        git(repo, "add", "-A"); git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "agent work")
        print("git status --porcelain after committing:", repr(git(repo, "status", "--porcelain")))
        print("budget check still sees the committed changes:", scope_check(repo, base, 3))
        print("a clean working tree does not mean nothing changed: the agent could have committed everything, so the comparison is against the recorded baseline commit and not against the current index")

        section("3. Genuinely checking: the dependency cache and what invalidates it")
        manifest = Path(d) / "requirements.txt"
        manifest.write_text("pytest\n", encoding="utf-8")
        now = time.time()
        cache = {"checked_at": now - 3600, "manifest_sha": sha(manifest), "runtime": "3.14", "result": "pass"}
        ttl = 24 * 3600
        print("fresh cache:", cache_valid(cache, manifest, now, ttl, "3.14"))
        print("23 days later:", cache_valid(cache, manifest, now + 23 * 86400, ttl, "3.14"))
        manifest.write_text("pytest\nrequests\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print("manifest edited ten minutes after the check:", cache_valid(cache, manifest, now + 600, ttl, "3.14"))
        manifest.write_text("pytest\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print("a different Python version:", cache_valid(cache, manifest, now, ttl, "3.12"))
        print("a time-to-live alone would have trusted the cache after the manifest changed; the cache is valid only while it is recent and the manifest and runtime it was computed for are unchanged")

        section("4. Genuinely running: a launcher that only starts the agent when the initializer exits zero")
        init_ok = "import sys; print('init ok'); sys.exit(0)"
        init_bad = "import sys; print('init BLOCKED: tests command missing'); sys.exit(1)"
        agent = "print('AGENT STARTED')"
        for label, init in (("healthy initializer", init_ok), ("blocked initializer", init_bad)):
            p1 = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", init], capture_output=True, text=True)
            started = False

            print(f"{label:20} initializer printed {p1.stdout.strip()!r:40} exit {p1.returncode} | agent started: {started}")

off_scope.","code":"def load_contract(path):
    try:
        c = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        raise ValueError(f"cannot read contract: {type(e).__name__}")
    if not isinstance(c, dict):
        raise ValueError("contract must be an object")
    missing = [k for k in REQUIRED if k not in c]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError("missing fields: " + ", ".join(missing))
    for k in ("task_id", "goal", "rollback_plan"):
        if not isinstance(c[k], str) or not c[k].strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{k} must be a non-empty string")
    for k in LISTS:
        if not isinstance(c[k], list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in c[k]):
            raise ValueError(f"{k} must be a list of strings")
    if not c["allowed_files"]:
        raise ValueError("allowed_files is empty: nothing could ever be in scope")
    return c


def norm(p):
    return p.replace("\\", "/")


def matches(path, pattern):
    path, pattern = norm(path), norm(pattern)
    if pattern.endswith("/**"):
        return path.startswith(pattern[:-3] + "/")
    return fnmatchcase(path, pattern)


def safe_path(p):
    parts = [x for x in norm(p).split("/") if x not in ("", ".")]
    if ".." in parts:
        return None
    return "/".join(parts)


def classify(path, contract):
    if any(matches(path, p) for p in contract["forbidden_files"]):
        return "forbidden"
    if any(matches(path, p) for p in contract["allowed_files"]):
        return "allowed"
    return "off_scope""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"sc_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() writes seven contracts to disk and loads each, classifies five paths against a contract whose allowlist overlaps its forbidden list, measures eight fnmatch cases, compares the recursive helper with plain fnmatch and sends four tricky paths through both the text match and safe_path.","descKn":"main() ಏಳು ಒಪ್ಪಂದಗಳನ್ನು ಡಿಸ್ಕ್‌ಗೆ ಬರೆದು ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದನ್ನು ಲೋಡ್ ಮಾಡಿ, ಅನುಮತಿ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ನಿಷೇಧ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಿಸುವ ಒಪ್ಪಂದದ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಐದು paths ವರ್ಗೀಕರಿಸಿ, ಎಂಟು fnmatch ಪ್ರಕರಣ ಅಳೆದು, ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಕ helper ಅನ್ನು ಸಾದಾ fnmatch ಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಕಷ್ಟದ paths ಅನ್ನು ಪಠ್ಯ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು safe_path ಎರಡರ ಮೂಲಕ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

        tests = [("src/auth/login.py", "src/*.py"), ("src/auth/login.py", "src/auth/*.py"), ("src/auth/deep/x.py", "src/auth/*.py"), ("tests/test_login.py", "tests/test_login*.py"),

off_scope.","code":"def load_contract(path):
    try:
        c = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        raise ValueError(f"cannot read contract: {type(e).__name__}")
    if not isinstance(c, dict):
        raise ValueError("contract must be an object")
    missing = [k for k in REQUIRED if k not in c]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError("missing fields: " + ", ".join(missing))
    for k in ("task_id", "goal", "rollback_plan"):
        if not isinstance(c[k], str) or not c[k].strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{k} must be a non-empty string")
    for k in LISTS:
        if not isinstance(c[k], list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in c[k]):
            raise ValueError(f"{k} must be a list of strings")
    if not c["allowed_files"]:
        raise ValueError("allowed_files is empty: nothing could ever be in scope")
    return c


def norm(p):
    return p.replace("\\", "/")


def matches(path, pattern):
    path, pattern = norm(path), norm(pattern)
    if pattern.endswith("/**"):
        return path.startswith(pattern[:-3] + "/")
    return fnmatchcase(path, pattern)


def safe_path(p):
    parts = [x for x in norm(p).split("/") if x not in ("", ".")]
    if ".." in parts:
        return None
    return "/".join(parts)


def classify(path, contract):
    if any(matches(path, p) for p in contract["forbidden_files"]):
        return "forbidden"
    if any(matches(path, p) for p in contract["allowed_files"]):
        return "allowed"
    return "off_scope""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"sc_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() writes seven contracts to disk and loads each, classifies five paths against a contract whose allowlist overlaps its forbidden list, measures eight fnmatch cases, compares the recursive helper with plain fnmatch and sends four tricky paths through both the text match and safe_path.","descKn":"main() ಏಳು ಒಪ್ಪಂದಗಳನ್ನು ಡಿಸ್ಕ್‌ಗೆ ಬರೆದು ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದನ್ನು ಲೋಡ್ ಮಾಡಿ, ಅನುಮತಿ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ನಿಷೇಧ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಿಸುವ ಒಪ್ಪಂದದ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಐದು paths ವರ್ಗೀಕರಿಸಿ, ಎಂಟು fnmatch ಪ್ರಕರಣ ಅಳೆದು, ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಕ helper ಅನ್ನು ಸಾದಾ fnmatch ಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಕಷ್ಟದ paths ಅನ್ನು ಪಠ್ಯ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು safe_path ಎರಡರ ಮೂಲಕ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

title: Scope Contracts and Task Boundaries (Part 2 of 3) — The Verification Gate
titleKn: ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ ಒಪ್ಪಂದಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಕಾರ್ಯ ಗಡಿಗಳು (ಭಾಗ 2 / 3) — ಪರಿಶೀಲನಾ Gate
desc: Combine scope, executed acceptance evidence, approvals and a time budget into one gate and test each check against a claim it should not trust.
objectives: Classify violations as error or warning.
Run acceptance commands, do not trust a list.
Require approver identity.
Enforce time in the runner.
Explain why one combination allows.
objectivesKn: ಉಲ್ಲಂಘನೆಗಳನ್ನು error ಅಥವಾ warning ಎಂದು ವರ್ಗೀಕರಿಸಿ.

    flag = [] if renames else ["--no-renames"]
    names = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", *flag, base).splitlines())
    names |= set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(names)


def classify(path, c):
    if any(matches(path, p) for p in c["forbidden_files"]):
        return "forbidden"
    return "allowed" if any(matches(path, p) for p in c["allowed_files"]) else "off_scope"


def verdict(files, c):
    bad = [f for f in files if classify(f, c) != "allowed"]
    return ("BLOCK" if bad else "ALLOW"), bad


def sha(p):

        print("verdict from the agent list:", verdict(agent_list, c0)[0], "| verdict from git:", verdict(real, c0))
        print("the agent list omitted the deploy script it edited and git's diff did not; the new test file was found because the check also asks for files git does not track yet, which git diff alone would miss")

        section("2. Genuinely measuring: a rename out of an allowed directory")

    names = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", *flag, base).splitlines())
    names |= set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(names)


def classify(path, c):
    if any(matches(path, p) for p in c["forbidden_files"]):
        return "forbidden"
    return "allowed" if any(matches(path, p) for p in c["allowed_files"]) else "off_scope"


def verdict(files, c):
    bad = [f for f in files if classify(f, c) != "allowed"]
    return ("BLOCK" if bad else "ALLOW"), bad


def sha(p):

    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    record = {"command": command, "started_at": started, "exit_code": None, "stdout": "", "stderr": "", "timed_out": False, "infrastructure_error": None}
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, cwd=cwd)
        record.update(exit_code=p.returncode, stdout=p.stdout, stderr=p.stderr)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        record.update(timed_out=True, stdout=(e.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(e.stdout, bytes) else (e.stdout or ""))
    except OSError as e:
        record["infrastructure_error"] = type(e).__name__
    record["duration_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
    return record


def classify(r):
    if r["infrastructure_error"]:
        return "could not launch"
    if r["timed_out"]:
        return "timed out"
    return "succeeded" if r["exit_code"] == 0 else f"failed (exit {r['exit_code']})"


def append_jsonl(path, record):
    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:

                 ("times out", [py, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(30)"]), ("missing program", ["no-such-program-xyz", "--version"])]

        r = run_with_feedback([py, "-I"] + disc[1:], cwd=empty)

        r2 = run_with_feedback([py, "-I"] + disc[1:], cwd=empty)
        print("empty tests directory, isolated:", classify(r2), "|", last(r2))

        r3 = run_with_feedback([py, "-I"] + disc[1:], cwd=empty)

    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    record = {"command": command, "started_at": started, "exit_code": None, "stdout": "", "stderr": "", "timed_out": False, "infrastructure_error": None}
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, cwd=cwd)
        record.update(exit_code=p.returncode, stdout=p.stdout, stderr=p.stderr)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        record.update(timed_out=True, stdout=(e.stdout or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(e.stdout, bytes) else (e.stdout or ""))
    except OSError as e:
        record["infrastructure_error"] = type(e).__name__
    record["duration_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
    return record


def classify(r):
    if r["infrastructure_error"]:
        return "could not launch"
    if r["timed_out"]:
        return "timed out"
    return "succeeded" if r["exit_code"] == 0 else f"failed (exit {r['exit_code']})"

BoundedCapture ತುಣುಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಿರ head buffer ಮತ್ತು ಜಾರುವ tail buffer ಗೆ ನೀಡಿ ಒಟ್ಟು ಎಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. redact ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಅಭಿವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಗಳ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def truncate_lines(text, head=5, tail=5):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if len(lines) <= head + tail:
        return text
    omitted = len(lines) - head - tail
    return chr(10).join(lines[:head] + [f"...truncated {omitted} lines..."] + lines[-tail:])


class BoundedCapture:
    def __init__(self, head_limit=2000, tail_limit=2000):
        self.head_limit, self.tail_limit = head_limit, tail_limit
        self.head, self.tail, self.total = bytearray(), bytearray(), 0

    def feed(self, chunk):
        self.total += len(chunk)
        room = self.head_limit - len(self.head)
        if room > 0:
            self.head += chunk[:room]
            chunk = chunk[room:]
        if chunk:
            self.tail += chunk
            if len(self.tail) > self.tail_limit:
                del self.tail[: len(self.tail) - self.tail_limit]

    def render(self):
        kept = len(self.head) + len(self.tail)
        mid = f"{chr(10)}...truncated {self.total - kept} bytes...{chr(10)}" if self.total > kept else ""
        return self.head.decode("utf-8", "replace") + mid + self.tail.decode("utf-8", "replace")


PATTERNS = [(re.compile(r"(?i)\bBearer\s+\S+"), "Bearer [REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(?i)\bpassword\s*=\s*\S+"), "password=[REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(?i)\bapi_key\s*=\s*\S+"), "api_key=[REDACTED]")]


def redact(text):
    for pat, rep in PATTERNS:
        text = pat.sub(rep, text)
    return text"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"fl_2.py","headingEn":"main(): six experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಆರು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() truncates a hundred lines, tries a five-million-character line, measures tracemalloc peaks for a child printing 20 MB, redacts four sample lines, tries five shapes of secret and compares a raw log with a redacted one.","descKn":"main() ನೂರು ಸಾಲು ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿ, ಐದು ಮಿಲಿಯನ್ ಅಕ್ಷರದ ಸಾಲು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, 20 MB ಮುದ್ರಿಸುವ child ಗೆ tracemalloc ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಅಳೆದು, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಮಾದರಿ ಸಾಲು ಮರೆಮಾಚಿ, ಐದು ರಹಸ್ಯ ಆಕಾರ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕಚ್ಚಾ ಲಾಗ್ ಅನ್ನು ಮರೆಮಾಚಿದ ಲಾಗ್‌ಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

    child = "import sys; [sys.stdout.write('y' * 99 + chr(10)) for _ in range(200000)]"

    p = subprocess.run([py, "-c", child], capture_output=True, text=True)

        cap.feed(chunk)
    proc.wait()

BoundedCapture ತುಣುಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಿರ head buffer ಮತ್ತು ಜಾರುವ tail buffer ಗೆ ನೀಡಿ ಒಟ್ಟು ಎಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. redact ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಅಭಿವ್ಯಕ್ತಿಗಳ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def truncate_lines(text, head=5, tail=5):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if len(lines) <= head + tail:
        return text
    omitted = len(lines) - head - tail
    return chr(10).join(lines[:head] + [f"...truncated {omitted} lines..."] + lines[-tail:])


class BoundedCapture:
    def __init__(self, head_limit=2000, tail_limit=2000):
        self.head_limit, self.tail_limit = head_limit, tail_limit
        self.head, self.tail, self.total = bytearray(), bytearray(), 0

    def feed(self, chunk):
        self.total += len(chunk)
        room = self.head_limit - len(self.head)
        if room > 0:
            self.head += chunk[:room]
            chunk = chunk[room:]
        if chunk:
            self.tail += chunk
            if len(self.tail) > self.tail_limit:
                del self.tail[: len(self.tail) - self.tail_limit]

    def render(self):
        kept = len(self.head) + len(self.tail)
        mid = f"{chr(10)}...truncated {self.total - kept} bytes...{chr(10)}" if self.total > kept else ""
        return self.head.decode("utf-8", "replace") + mid + self.tail.decode("utf-8", "replace")


PATTERNS = [(re.compile(r"(?i)\bBearer\s+\S+"), "Bearer [REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(?i)\bpassword\s*=\s*\S+"), "password=[REDACTED]"), (re.compile(r"(?i)\bapi_key\s*=\s*\S+"), "api_key=[REDACTED]")]


def redact(text):
    for pat, rep in PATTERNS:
        text = pat.sub(rep, text)

ಮರುಹೆಸರಿಸಿ ಹಳೆಯದನ್ನು ಬಿಡುತ್ತದೆ. chain ಕೊನೆಯ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನದಿಂದ parent ids ಹಿಂಬಾಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. gate ಕಾಣೆಯಾದ, ಹಳೆಯ ಅಥವಾ ವಿಫಲ ದಾಖಲೆ ನಿರಾಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def run(command, cwd, parent=None, timeout=60):
    t0 = time.time()
    p = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout)
    return {"command_id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "parent_command_id": parent, "command": command, "exit_code": p.returncode, "stdout": p.stdout[-300:], "stderr": p.stderr[-300:],
            "finished_at": time.time(), "duration_ms": round((time.time() - t0) * 1000)}


def append_rotating(path, record, max_bytes=400, keep=3):
    path = Path(path)
    line = json.dumps(record) + chr(10)
    if path.exists() and path.stat().st_size + len(line.encode("utf-8")) > max_bytes:
        for i in range(keep, 0, -1):
            src = path if i == 1 else path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{i - 1}")
            dst = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{i}")
            if src.exists():
                if dst.exists():
                    dst.unlink()
                src.rename(dst)
    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(line)


def read_records(path):
    good, bad = [], 0
    for ln in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        try:
            good.append(json.loads(ln))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            bad += 1
    return good, bad


def chain(records, last_id):
    by_id = {r["command_id"]: r for r in records}
    out, cur = [], by_id.get(last_id)
    while cur:
        out.append(cur["command_id"])
        cur = by_id.get(cur["parent_command_id"])
    return list(reversed(out))


def gate(records, expected_command, newest_edit_time):
    matching = [r for r in records if r["command"] == expected_command]
    if not matching:
        return "BLOCK", "no record for the required command"
    last = matching[-1]
    if last["finished_at"] < newest_edit_time:
        return "BLOCK", "the record is older than the latest edit"
    if last["exit_code"] != 0:
        return "BLOCK", f"exit code {last['exit_code']}"
    return "ALLOW", "fresh record with exit code 0""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"fl_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() writes twenty records through a 400-byte rotating log, appends a half-written line and reads the file, builds a three-attempt retry chain plus an unrelated command, gates three situations and runs a failing test, applies a one-character fix and reruns, with and without clearing the bytecode cache.","descKn":"main() ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು 400-ಬೈಟ್ rotating ಲಾಗ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಬರೆದು, ಅರ್ಧ ಬರೆದ ಸಾಲು ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಫೈಲ್ ಓದಿ, ಮೂರು-ಪ್ರಯತ್ನದ ಮರುಪ್ರಯತ್ನ ಸರಪಳಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಬಂಧವಿಲ್ಲದ ಆದೇಶ ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ಸಂದರ್ಭಗಳನ್ನು gate ಮಾಡಿ, ವಿಫಲ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಒಂದು-ಅಕ್ಷರ ಸರಿಪಡಿಕೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿ ಬೈಟ್‌ಕೋಡ್ ಕ್ಯಾಶ್ ತೆರವಿನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತು ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಮರುಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        base = Path(d)

        section("1. Genuinely running: rotation bounds the log")
        log = base / "feedback_record.jsonl"
        for i in range(20):
            append_rotating(log, {"i": i, "pad": "x" * 60})
        files = sorted(p.name for p in base.glob("feedback_record.jsonl*"))
        counts = {n: len((base / n).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()) for n in files}
        print("files:", files)
        print("records per file:", counts, "| total kept:", sum(counts.values()), "of 20 written")
        print("the newest records stayed in the live file and the oldest were dropped when the backups ran out, so storage is bounded; the dropped records are gone for good, and anything that must be kept longer needs separate retention")

        section("2. Genuinely running: a partial last line and the reader")
        with open(log, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write('{"i": 99, "pad": "tru')
        good, bad = read_records(log)
        print("readable records:", len(good), "| damaged lines skipped and counted:", bad)
        print("a crash in the middle of an append left a broken last line; the reader kept every complete record in the live file and reported one damaged line instead of failing on the whole file")

        section("3. Genuinely running: command_id and parent_command_id rebuild a retry history")
        proj = base / "proj"
        proj.mkdir()
        (proj / "m.py").write_text("print(1)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        a = run([PY, "-c", "import sys; sys.exit(1)"], proj)
        b = run([PY, "-c", "import sys; sys.exit(1)"], proj, parent=a["command_id"])
        c = run([PY, "-c", "print('ok')"], proj, parent=b["command_id"])
        other = run([PY, "-c", "print('unrelated')"], proj)
        recs = [a, b, c, other]
        print("attempt exit codes:", [r["exit_code"] for r in (a, b, c)])
        print("chain for the last attempt:", [recs.index(next(r for r in recs if r["command_id"] == i)) for i in chain(recs, c["command_id"])], "of", len(recs), "records; the unrelated command is not in it:", other["command_id"] not in chain(recs, c["command_id"]))
        print("following parents from the last attempt recovered the two failures and the success in order, without mixing in an unrelated command, which is what a reviewer needs to see that the pass came after two failures")

        section("4. Genuinely running: the gate over records, including missing and stale evidence")
        test_cmd = [PY, "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"]
        (proj / "tests").mkdir()
        (proj / "tests" / "test_m.py").write_text("import unittest" + chr(10) + "class T(unittest.TestCase):" + chr(10) + "    def test_a(self):" + chr(10) + "        self.assertTrue(True)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        edit_time = time.time()
        print("no record yet:", gate([], test_cmd, edit_time))
        time.sleep(0.05)
        r = run([PY, "-I", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"], proj)
        gated = [dict(r, command=test_cmd)]
        print("record from -I run labelled with the required command:", gate(gated, test_cmd, edit_time))
        later_edit = time.time() + 1
        print("same record after a later edit:", gate(gated, test_cmd, later_edit))
        print("the gate refused a missing record, accepted a fresh zero exit and refused the same record once the code had changed after it ran; a command that passed before the last edit says nothing about the code now (this lab relabelled the record to keep the gate simple, which a real runner must not do)")

        section("5. Genuinely running: a scripted failure and repair on real code")
        work = base / "discount"
        (work / "tests").mkdir(parents=True)
        (work / "calc.py").write_text("def discount(price, pct):" + chr(10) + "    return price + price * pct / 100" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "tests" / "test_calc.py").write_text("import unittest, sys, os" + chr(10) + "sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())" + chr(10) + "from calc import discount" + chr(10) + "class T(unittest.TestCase):" + chr(10) + "    def test_ten_percent(self):" + chr(10) + "        self.assertEqual(discount(200, 10), 180)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        cmd = [PY, "-I", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"]
        first = run(cmd, work)
        print("first run: exit", first["exit_code"], "| evidence:", [x for x in first["stderr"].splitlines() if "AssertionError" in x])
        text = (work / "calc.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "calc.py").write_text(text.replace("price + price", "price - price"), encoding="utf-8")
        second = run(cmd, work, parent=first["command_id"])
        print("after the scripted fix: exit", second["exit_code"], "| evidence:", [x for x in second["stderr"].splitlines() if "AssertionError" in x] or "none", "| parent is the first run:", second["parent_command_id"] == first["command_id"])
        import shutil
        shutil.rmtree(work / "__pycache__", ignore_errors=True)
        third = run(cmd, work, parent=second["command_id"])
        print("after deleting __pycache__: exit", third["exit_code"], "| chain:", [first["exit_code"], second["exit_code"], third["exit_code"]])
        print("the correct one-character edit still failed with the old assertion value when the test was rerun immediately, which is consistent with stale cached bytecode (the edit kept the file size and landed in the same second; the cause was not inspected directly), and it passed once __pycache__ was removed; on this machine, in three repeated runs, this happened every time; the evidence was real but stale, so a feedback runner should disable or clear bytecode caches when it verifies a change; the stand-in applied one fixed edit, so this shows loop mechanics and not that a real model could find the fix")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

gate refuses a missing, stale or failing record.","descKn":"run ಪ್ರತಿ ದಾಖಲೆಗೆ command_id ಮತ್ತು parent_command_id ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. append_rotating ಗಾತ್ರ ಮಿತಿ ಮೀರುವಾಗ ಲೈವ್ ಫೈಲ್ ಅನ್ನು ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಬ್ಯಾಕಪ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಮರುಹೆಸರಿಸಿ ಹಳೆಯದನ್ನು ಬಿಡುತ್ತದೆ. chain ಕೊನೆಯ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನದಿಂದ parent ids ಹಿಂಬಾಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. gate ಕಾಣೆಯಾದ, ಹಳೆಯ ಅಥವಾ ವಿಫಲ ದಾಖಲೆ ನಿರಾಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def run(command, cwd, parent=None, timeout=60):
    t0 = time.time()
    p = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout)
    return {"command_id": uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], "parent_command_id": parent, "command": command, "exit_code": p.returncode, "stdout": p.stdout[-300:], "stderr": p.stderr[-300:],
            "finished_at": time.time(), "duration_ms": round((time.time() - t0) * 1000)}


def append_rotating(path, record, max_bytes=400, keep=3):
    path = Path(path)
    line = json.dumps(record) + chr(10)
    if path.exists() and path.stat().st_size + len(line.encode("utf-8")) > max_bytes:
        for i in range(keep, 0, -1):
            src = path if i == 1 else path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{i - 1}")
            dst = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{i}")
            if src.exists():
                if dst.exists():
                    dst.unlink()
                src.rename(dst)
    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(line)


def read_records(path):
    good, bad = [], 0
    for ln in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        try:
            good.append(json.loads(ln))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            bad += 1
    return good, bad


def chain(records, last_id):
    by_id = {r["command_id"]: r for r in records}
    out, cur = [], by_id.get(last_id)
    while cur:
        out.append(cur["command_id"])
        cur = by_id.get(cur["parent_command_id"])
    return list(reversed(out))


def gate(records, expected_command, newest_edit_time):
    matching = [r for r in records if r["command"] == expected_command]
    if not matching:
        return "BLOCK", "no record for the required command"
    last = matching[-1]
    if last["finished_at"] < newest_edit_time:
        return "BLOCK", "the record is older than the latest edit"
    if last["exit_code"] != 0:
        return "BLOCK", f"exit code {last['exit_code']}"
    return "ALLOW", "fresh record with exit code 0""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"fl_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() writes twenty records through a 400-byte rotating log, appends a half-written line and reads the file, builds a three-attempt retry chain plus an unrelated command, gates three situations and runs a failing test, applies a one-character fix and reruns, with and without clearing the bytecode cache.","descKn":"main() ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು 400-ಬೈಟ್ rotating ಲಾಗ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಬರೆದು, ಅರ್ಧ ಬರೆದ ಸಾಲು ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಫೈಲ್ ಓದಿ, ಮೂರು-ಪ್ರಯತ್ನದ ಮರುಪ್ರಯತ್ನ ಸರಪಳಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಬಂಧವಿಲ್ಲದ ಆದೇಶ ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ಸಂದರ್ಭಗಳನ್ನು gate ಮಾಡಿ, ವಿಫಲ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಒಂದು-ಅಕ್ಷರ ಸರಿಪಡಿಕೆ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿ ಬೈಟ್‌ಕೋಡ್ ಕ್ಯಾಶ್ ತೆರವಿನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತು ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಮರುಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        base = Path(d)

        section("1. Genuinely running: rotation bounds the log")
        log = base / "feedback_record.jsonl"
        for i in range(20):
            append_rotating(log, {"i": i, "pad": "x" * 60})
        files = sorted(p.name for p in base.glob("feedback_record.jsonl*"))
        counts = {n: len((base / n).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()) for n in files}
        print("files:", files)
        print("records per file:", counts, "| total kept:", sum(counts.values()), "of 20 written")
        print("the newest records stayed in the live file and the oldest were dropped when the backups ran out, so storage is bounded; the dropped records are gone for good, and anything that must be kept longer needs separate retention")

        section("2. Genuinely running: a partial last line and the reader")
        with open(log, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write('{"i": 99, "pad": "tru')
        good, bad = read_records(log)
        print("readable records:", len(good), "| damaged lines skipped and counted:", bad)
        print("a crash in the middle of an append left a broken last line; the reader kept every complete record in the live file and reported one damaged line instead of failing on the whole file")

        section("3. Genuinely running: command_id and parent_command_id rebuild a retry history")
        proj = base / "proj"
        proj.mkdir()
        (proj / "m.py").write_text("print(1)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        a = run([PY, "-c", "import sys; sys.exit(1)"], proj)
        b = run([PY, "-c", "import sys; sys.exit(1)"], proj, parent=a["command_id"])
        c = run([PY, "-c", "print('ok')"], proj, parent=b["command_id"])
        other = run([PY, "-c", "print('unrelated')"], proj)
        recs = [a, b, c, other]
        print("attempt exit codes:", [r["exit_code"] for r in (a, b, c)])
        print("chain for the last attempt:", [recs.index(next(r for r in recs if r["command_id"] == i)) for i in chain(recs, c["command_id"])], "of", len(recs), "records; the unrelated command is not in it:", other["command_id"] not in chain(recs, c["command_id"]))
        print("following parents from the last attempt recovered the two failures and the success in order, without mixing in an unrelated command, which is what a reviewer needs to see that the pass came after two failures")

        section("4. Genuinely running: the gate over records, including missing and stale evidence")
        test_cmd = [PY, "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"]
        (proj / "tests").mkdir()
        (proj / "tests" / "test_m.py").write_text("import unittest" + chr(10) + "class T(unittest.TestCase):" + chr(10) + "    def test_a(self):" + chr(10) + "        self.assertTrue(True)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        edit_time = time.time()
        print("no record yet:", gate([], test_cmd, edit_time))
        time.sleep(0.05)
        r = run([PY, "-I", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"], proj)
        gated = [dict(r, command=test_cmd)]
        print("record from -I run labelled with the required command:", gate(gated, test_cmd, edit_time))
        later_edit = time.time() + 1
        print("same record after a later edit:", gate(gated, test_cmd, later_edit))
        print("the gate refused a missing record, accepted a fresh zero exit and refused the same record once the code had changed after it ran; a command that passed before the last edit says nothing about the code now (this lab relabelled the record to keep the gate simple, which a real runner must not do)")

        section("5. Genuinely running: a scripted failure and repair on real code")
        work = base / "discount"
        (work / "tests").mkdir(parents=True)
        (work / "calc.py").write_text("def discount(price, pct):" + chr(10) + "    return price + price * pct / 100" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "tests" / "test_calc.py").write_text("import unittest, sys, os" + chr(10) + "sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())" + chr(10) + "from calc import discount" + chr(10) + "class T(unittest.TestCase):" + chr(10) + "    def test_ten_percent(self):" + chr(10) + "        self.assertEqual(discount(200, 10), 180)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        cmd = [PY, "-I", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"]
        first = run(cmd, work)
        print("first run: exit", first["exit_code"], "| evidence:", [x for x in first["stderr"].splitlines() if "AssertionError" in x])
        text = (work / "calc.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "calc.py").write_text(text.replace("price + price", "price - price"), encoding="utf-8")
        second = run(cmd, work, parent=first["command_id"])
        print("after the scripted fix: exit", second["exit_code"], "| evidence:", [x for x in second["stderr"].splitlines() if "AssertionError" in x] or "none", "| parent is the first run:", second["parent_command_id"] == first["command_id"])
        import shutil
        shutil.rmtree(work / "__pycache__", ignore_errors=True)
        third = run(cmd, work, parent=second["command_id"])
        print("after deleting __pycache__: exit", third["exit_code"], "| chain:", [first["exit_code"], second["exit_code"], third["exit_code"]])
        print("the correct one-character edit still failed with the old assertion value when the test was rerun immediately, which is consistent with stale cached bytecode (the edit kept the file size and landed in the same second; the cause was not inspected directly), and it passed once __pycache__ was removed; on this machine, in three repeated runs, this happened every time; the evidence was real but stale, so a feedback runner should disable or clear bytecode caches when it verifies a change; the stand-in applied one fixed edit, so this shows loop mechanics and not that a real model could find the fix")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    findings = []

    def add(code, sev, msg):
        findings.append({"code": code, "severity": sev, "message": msg})

    for cmd in REQUIRED:
        recs = [r for r in art["feedback"] if r["command"] == cmd]
        if not recs:
            add("ACCEPTANCE_NOT_RUN", "block", f"Missing execution evidence: {cmd}")
        elif recs[-1]["exit_code"] != 0:
            add("ACCEPTANCE_FAILED", "block", f"{cmd} exited {recs[-1]['exit_code']}")
    for f in art["touched"]:
        if f not in art["scope"]["allowed"]:
            add("SCOPE_VIOLATION", "block", f"{f} is outside the allowed files")
    for rule in art["rules"]:
        if not rule["ok"]:
            add("RULE_" + rule["id"], rule["severity"], rule["message"])
    if strict:
        for f in findings:
            if f["severity"] == "warn":
                f["severity"] = "block"
    findings.sort(key=lambda f: (f["code"], f["message"]))
    return {"task_id": task_id, "passed": not any(f["severity"] == "block" for f in findings), "findings": findings}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"vg_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() runs the lesson's scenarios, compares normal and strict policy, checks verdict against findings, shuffles evidence 200 times and hands the gate a scope that allows an authentication file.","descKn":"main() lesson ನ ಸನ್ನಿವೇಶಗಳನ್ನು ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು strict ನೀತಿ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ತೀರ್ಪನ್ನು findings ಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯವನ್ನು 200 ಬಾರಿ ಕಲಸಿ, ಮತ್ತು authentication ಫೈಲ್ ಅನುಮತಿಸುವ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಯನ್ನು gate ಗೆ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the three scenarios of the lesson")
    show("clean pass", verify("T1", clean()))
    a = clean(); a["feedback"] = []
    show("acceptance never run", verify("T1", a))
    b = clean(); b["touched"].append("src/auth.py")
    show("unauthorised file touched", verify("T1", b))
    c = clean(); c["feedback"][0]["exit_code"] = 1
    show("acceptance command failed", verify("T1", c))
    print("the agent's own statement never appears as an input: the gate saw only records, the scope, the diff and the rule results, so a claim of 'done' could not change any verdict above")

    section("2. Genuinely running: a warning passes under normal policy and blocks in strict mode")
    w = clean(); w["rules"] = [{"id": "DOCS", "ok": False, "severity": "warn", "message": "docs not updated"}]
    show("normal policy", verify("T1", w))
    show("strict policy", verify("T1", w, strict=True))
    print("the same evidence gave different verdicts under two policies, which is correct: the policy is an explicit input, and strict mode is how a team promotes warnings to blockers without editing the rules")

    section("3. Genuinely checking: the verdict cannot contradict its findings")
    cases = [clean(), a, b, c, w]
    ok = all(verify("T", x)["passed"] == (not any(f["severity"] == "block" for f in verify("T", x)["findings"])) for x in cases)
    print("passed equals 'no block finding' for every case:", ok)
    print("passed is computed from the findings and never stored separately, so a report that says passed with a blocking finding, or failed with none, cannot be produced by this function")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: determinism over shuffled and repeated input")
    base = clean()
    base["touched"] = ["src/pay.py", "x.py", "y.py"]
    base["rules"] = [{"id": f"R{i}", "ok": False, "severity": "warn", "message": f"m{i}"} for i in range(5)]
    outs = set()
    rnd = random.Random(7)
    for _ in range(200):
        x = json.loads(json.dumps(base))
        rnd.shuffle(x["touched"]); rnd.shuffle(x["rules"])
        outs.add(json.dumps(verify("T", x), sort_keys=True))
    print("distinct reports from 200 shuffles of the same evidence:", len(outs))
    print("findings are sorted by code and message before the report is built, so the order of the evidence does not change the report; identical inputs and policy give byte-identical JSON, which makes the report diffable and cacheable")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: determinism is not correctness")
    weak = clean(); weak["rules"] = []
    weak["touched"] = ["src/pay.py", "src/auth.py"]
    weak["scope"] = {"allowed": ["src/pay.py", "src/auth.py"]}
    show("a scope contract that allows auth", verify("T1", weak))
    print("the gate returned the same pass every time for a task that was told not to touch authentication, because the scope it was handed allowed it; a deterministic gate faithfully applies whatever policy it receives, so the policy needs its own review")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    ok = all(verify("T", x)["passed"] == (not any(f["severity"] == "block" for f in verify("T", x)["findings"])) for x in cases)

    print("passed is computed from the findings and never stored separately, so a report that says passed with a blocking finding, or failed with none, cannot be produced by this function")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: determinism over shuffled and repeated input")
    base = clean()
    base["touched"] = ["src/pay.py", "x.py", "y.py"]
    base["rules"] = [{"id": f"R{i}", "ok": False, "severity": "warn", "message": f"m{i}"} for i in range(5)]

    for _ in range(200):
        x = json.loads(json.dumps(base))
        rnd.shuffle(x["touched"]); rnd.shuffle(x["rules"])

def validate(rec, task_id, revision):
    errs = []
    if not isinstance(rec, dict):
        return ["record is not an object"]
    for k in ("command", "exit_code", "task_id", "revision"):
        if k not in rec:
            errs.append(f"missing {k}")
    if errs:
        return errs
    if not isinstance(rec["command"], str):
        errs.append("command must be a string")
    if not valid_exit(rec["exit_code"]):
        errs.append(f"exit_code must be an int, got {type(rec['exit_code']).__name__}")
    if rec["task_id"] != task_id:
        errs.append("record belongs to another task")
    if rec["revision"] != revision:
        errs.append("record is for another revision")
    return errs


def verify(records, task_id, revision, normalise=False):
    findings, valid = [], []
    for i, r in enumerate(records):
        e = validate(r, task_id, revision)
        if e:
            findings.append(("EVIDENCE_INVALID", i, e[0]))
        else:
            valid.append(r)
    key = (lambda s: " ".join(s.split())) if normalise else (lambda s: s)
    m = [r for r in valid if key(r["command"]) == key(CMD)]
    if not m:
        findings.append(("ACCEPTANCE_NOT_RUN", None, CMD))
    elif m[-1]["exit_code"] != 0:
        findings.append(("ACCEPTANCE_FAILED", None, str(m[-1]["exit_code"])))

ದಾಖಲೆಯನ್ನು finding ಆಗಿ ವರದಿ ಮಾಡಿ, ಮಾನ್ಯವಾದವುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅಗತ್ಯ ಆದೇಶ ಹೊಂದಿಸಿ ಕೊನೆಯ ಹೊಂದುವ ದಾಖಲೆ ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def valid_exit(v):
    return type(v) is int


def validate(rec, task_id, revision):
    errs = []
    if not isinstance(rec, dict):
        return ["record is not an object"]
    for k in ("command", "exit_code", "task_id", "revision"):
        if k not in rec:
            errs.append(f"missing {k}")
    if errs:
        return errs
    if not isinstance(rec["command"], str):
        errs.append("command must be a string")
    if not valid_exit(rec["exit_code"]):
        errs.append(f"exit_code must be an int, got {type(rec['exit_code']).__name__}")
    if rec["task_id"] != task_id:
        errs.append("record belongs to another task")
    if rec["revision"] != revision:
        errs.append("record is for another revision")
    return errs


def verify(records, task_id, revision, normalise=False):
    findings, valid = [], []
    for i, r in enumerate(records):
        e = validate(r, task_id, revision)
        if e:
            findings.append(("EVIDENCE_INVALID", i, e[0]))
        else:
            valid.append(r)
    key = (lambda s: " ".join(s.split())) if normalise else (lambda s: s)
    m = [r for r in valid if key(r["command"]) == key(CMD)]
    if not m:
        findings.append(("ACCEPTANCE_NOT_RUN", None, CMD))
    elif m[-1]["exit_code"] != 0:
        findings.append(("ACCEPTANCE_FAILED", None, str(m[-1]["exit_code"])))
    return not findings, findings"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"vg_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() compares six values with zero, feeds six malformed or valid records, varies task and revision, varies the command text and runs a small gate script as a subprocess on four evidence files.","descKn":"main() ಆರು ಮೌಲ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಸೊನ್ನೆಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಆರು ದೋಷಪೂರ್ಣ ಅಥವಾ ಮಾನ್ಯ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ನೀಡಿ, task ಮತ್ತು revision ಬದಲಿಸಿ, ಆದೇಶ ಪಠ್ಯ ಬದಲಿಸಿ, ಮತ್ತು ಸಣ್ಣ gate ಸ್ಕ್ರಿಪ್ಟ್ ಅನ್ನು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಫೈಲ್‌ಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ subprocess ಆಗಿ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely checking: values Python treats as 0 and what a type check does with them")
    for label, v in (("int 0", 0), ("bool False", False), ("str '0'", "0"), ("float 0.0", 0.0), ("None", None), ("bool True", True)):
        loose = v == 0
        print(f"{label:11} == 0: {loose!s:5} | isinstance int: {isinstance(v, int)!s:5} | strict type is int: {valid_exit(v)}")
    print("False == 0 and isinstance(False, int) are both true in Python, so a validator that only checks isinstance accepts a boolean as an exit code, and a loose comparison accepts 0.0 as success; the strict test type(v) is int rejects all of them except a real integer")

    section("2. Genuinely running: malformed records fail closed")
    cases = [("valid", rec()), ("exit_code is False", rec(exit_code=False)), ("exit_code is '0'", rec(exit_code="0")), ("exit_code is None", rec(exit_code=None)),
             ("missing revision", {k: v for k, v in rec().items() if k != "revision"}), ("not an object", "ok")]
    for label, r in cases:
        ok, f = verify([r], "T", "r2")
        print(f"{label:20} passed={ok!s:5} {f[:2]}")
    print("every malformed record produced an invalid-evidence finding and, because it was excluded from the valid set, an acceptance-not-run finding as well; the gate did not guess what the writer meant")

    section("3. Genuinely running: identity and revision")
    print("evidence for another task      :", verify([rec(task_id="OTHER")], "T", "r2")[0])
    print("pass recorded on an older revision:", verify([rec(revision="r1")], "T", "r2")[0])
    print("old pass then new failure       :", verify([rec(revision="r1"), rec(exit_code=1)], "T", "r2"))
    print("old failure then new pass       :", verify([rec(revision="r1", exit_code=1), rec()], "T", "r2")[0])
    print("same revision, fail then pass    :", verify([rec(exit_code=1), rec()], "T", "r2")[0], "| same revision, pass then fail:", verify([rec(), rec(exit_code=1)], "T", "r2")[0])
    print("a pass for another task or an older revision was not accepted as proof; this gate also reports every stale record as invalid evidence, so a stale record next to a valid final pass still blocked (the 'old failure then new pass' line), which is strict but noisy, and a gate that filters by revision first would pass; with two records for the final revision the last one decided; each of these is a policy choice that has to be written down")

    section("4. Genuinely running: how exactly the command must match")
    for label, c in (("exact", CMD), ("double space", "python  -m unittest"), ("trailing space", CMD + " "), ("different flags", CMD + " -v")):
        print(f"{label:16} exact match -> {verify([rec(command=c)], 'T', 'r2')[0]!s:5} | whitespace-normalised -> {verify([rec(command=c)], 'T', 'r2', normalise=True)[0]}")
    print("a harmless double space failed the exact match, and normalising whitespace fixed that without accepting a command with extra flags; whether -v counts is a policy decision, because flags may change what is run")

    section("5. Genuinely running: the command-line exit codes through a real subprocess")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        prog = Path(d) / "gate.py"
        prog.write_text("import json, sys" + chr(10) + "try:" + chr(10) + "    data = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))" + chr(10) + "    assert isinstance(data, list) and all(isinstance(x, dict) for x in data)" + chr(10) +
                        "except Exception:" + chr(10) + "    print('evidence unreadable'); sys.exit(2)" + chr(10) +
                        "ok = any(x.get('command') == 'python -m unittest' and type(x.get('exit_code')) is int and x['exit_code'] == 0 for x in data)" + chr(10) +
                        "print('PASS' if ok else 'BLOCK'); sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        for label, payload in (("good evidence", json.dumps([rec()])), ("failing evidence", json.dumps([rec(exit_code=1)])), ("corrupt file", "{not json"), ("wrong shape", json.dumps({"a": 1}))):
            f = Path(d) / "ev.json"
            f.write_text(payload, encoding="utf-8")
            p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(prog), str(f)], capture_output=True, text=True)
            print(f"{label:17} printed {p.stdout.strip():18} exit code {p.returncode}")
    print("0 means verified, 1 means verified and blocked, and 2 means the evidence could not be read; keeping 2 separate lets a CI job tell 'the work is not done' from 'the gate could not decide', and both stop the pipeline")
    print("NaN check for reference:", math.isnan(float('nan')), "- numeric evidence such as coverage needs the same strictness, which the next part applies")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

scope_vs_diff(reported, repo, base):
    actual = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", base).splitlines()) | set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(actual - set(reported)), sorted(set(reported) - actual)


def coverage_rule(prev, cur, max_drop=1.0):
    for label, v in (("previous", prev), ("current", cur)):
        if type(v) not in (int, float) or isinstance(v, bool) or math.isnan(v) or not 0 <= v <= 100:
            return "block", f"{label} coverage is not a number from 0 to 100"
    return ("block", f"coverage fell {prev - cur:.1f} points") if prev - cur > max_drop else ("pass", "within tolerance")


def sign(override):
    msg = json.dumps({k: override[k] for k in ("task_id", "code", "expires")}, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hmac.new(KEY, msg, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def apply_override(finding, override, task_id, now):
    if override.get("task_id") != task_id or override.get("code") != finding["code"]:
        return False, "override is for another task or finding"
    if override["expires"] < now:
        return False, "override expired"
    if not hmac.compare_digest(sign(override), override.get("sig", "")):
        return False, "signature does not match"
    if finding["code"] in ("SCOPE_VIOLATION", "ACCEPTANCE_FAILED"):
        return False, "this finding cannot be overridden"
    return True, "override accepted"

    return not any(f["severity"] == "block" for f in findings)

scope_vs_diff(reported, repo, base):
    actual = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", base).splitlines()) | set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(actual - set(reported)), sorted(set(reported) - actual)


def coverage_rule(prev, cur, max_drop=1.0):
    for label, v in (("previous", prev), ("current", cur)):
        if type(v) not in (int, float) or isinstance(v, bool) or math.isnan(v) or not 0 <= v <= 100:
            return "block", f"{label} coverage is not a number from 0 to 100"
    return ("block", f"coverage fell {prev - cur:.1f} points") if prev - cur > max_drop else ("pass", "within tolerance")


def sign(override):
    msg = json.dumps({k: override[k] for k in ("task_id", "code", "expires")}, sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hmac.new(KEY, msg, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def apply_override(finding, override, task_id, now):
    if override.get("task_id") != task_id or override.get("code") != finding["code"]:
        return False, "override is for another task or finding"
    if override["expires"] < now:
        return False, "override expired"
    if not hmac.compare_digest(sign(override), override.get("sig", "")):
        return False, "signature does not match"
    if finding["code"] in ("SCOPE_VIOLATION", "ACCEPTANCE_FAILED"):
        return False, "this finding cannot be overridden"
    return True, "override accepted"


GATE_SRC = '''
def gate(findings):
    return not any(f["severity"] == "block" for f in findings)
'''
TESTS = [([], True), ([{"severity": "warn"}], True), ([{"severity": "block"}], False), ([{"severity": "warn"}, {"severity": "block"}], False)]


def run_tests(src):
    ns = {}
    exec(src, ns)
    return [ns["gate"](f) == want for f, want in TESTS]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"vg_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() builds a temporary git repository, tries seven coverage inputs, five overrides, four mutants of a two-line gate and the same mutants against a weaker suite.","descKn":"main() ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ git repository ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ, ಏಳು coverage ಇನ್‌ಪುಟ್, ಐದು overrides, ಎರಡು-ಸಾಲಿನ gate ನ ನಾಲ್ಕು mutants ಮತ್ತು ಅದೇ mutants ಅನ್ನು ದುರ್ಬಲ ಸೂಟ್ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        repo = Path(d) / "repo"
        repo.mkdir()
        git(repo, "init", "-q")

        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
        base = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()

        section("1. Genuinely running: the reported touched files against the real git diff")
        (repo / "src/pay.py").write_text("v2" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (repo / "src/auth.py").write_text("new" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        unreported, phantom = scope_vs_diff(["src/pay.py", "tests/test_pay.py"], repo, base)
        print("changed in git but not reported:", unreported)
        print("reported but not changed in git:", phantom)
        print("both kinds of mismatch are findings: an unreported change is a hidden edit and a reported file that never changed is a claim with nothing behind it; the scope report is a derived assessment, and the diff is the evidence it must agree with")

    section("2. Genuinely running: coverage regression with numeric validation")
    for label, prev, cur in (("85 to 85", 85, 85), ("85 to 84.5", 85, 84.5), ("85 to 83", 85, 83), ("85 to NaN", 85, float("nan")), ("85 to True", 85, True), ("85 to '90'", 85, "90"), ("85 to 120", 85, 120)):
        print(f"{label:12} {coverage_rule(prev, cur)}")
    print("a drop within the tolerance passed and a larger one blocked; NaN fails every comparison, so without the explicit check a NaN coverage would not have looked like a drop at all, and booleans and strings are rejected like exit codes were; the baseline itself is trusted input and has to come from the protected branch")
    print("what a bare comparison says for NaN:", float("nan") < 80, float("nan") > 80)

    section("3. Genuinely running: signed overrides")
    now = time.time()
    finding = {"code": "RULE_DOCS"}

    ov["sig"] = sign(ov)
    print("valid override:", apply_override(finding, ov, "T", now))
    print("other task    :", apply_override(finding, ov, "OTHER", now))
    print("expired       :", apply_override(finding, ov, "T", now + 7200))
    t = dict(ov, expires=now + 10 ** 6)
    print("expiry edited :", apply_override(finding, t, "T", now))
    blocked = {"task_id": "T", "code": "SCOPE_VIOLATION", "expires": now + 3600}
    blocked["sig"] = sign(blocked)
    print("scope finding :", apply_override({"code": "SCOPE_VIOLATION"}, blocked, "T", now))
    print("a correctly signed, in-date override for the right finding was accepted, and editing the expiry broke the signature; policy also refuses to override a scope violation even when validly signed; the key here is a made-up constant in the lab, and a real key must be held outside the agent's reach")

    section("4. Genuinely running: testing the gate itself by mutation")

    for name, src in mutants.items():

        print(f"{name:20} tests: {res} -> {'caught' if not all(res) else 'SURVIVED'}")
    print("each of four deliberate breakages made at least one test fail, so these four tests are enough to notice them; this is four hand-made mutants of a two-line function, not a measure of coverage, and the missing-evidence and malformed-evidence paths would need their own tests")

        print(f"{name:20} survives a suite that only has the pass cases: {all(res)}")
    print("with only the two passing scenarios, one of the four mutants (always true) survived and the other three were still caught because they also changed a passing outcome; a gate that always allows is only caught by a case that should block, which is the case the gate exists for")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

title: Reviewer Agent (Part 1 of 3) — The Rubric and Verdict
titleKn: Reviewer Agent (ಭಾಗ 1 / 3) — Rubric ಮತ್ತು ತೀರ್ಪು
desc: Build five rubric scorers and a verdict engine with a hard-fail rule, and see a passing gate still fail review.
objectives: Score five dimensions with findings.
Apply the hard-fail rule.
Reject non-integer scores.
Separate gate from reviewer.
Write the report as evidence.
objectivesKn: ಐದು ಆಯಾಮಗಳಿಗೆ findings ಜೊತೆ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡಿ.

title: Reviewer Agent (Part 2 of 3) — Independent Evidence and Rubric Policy
titleKn: Reviewer Agent (ಭಾಗ 2 / 3) — ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು Rubric ನೀತಿ
desc: Compare a flag-reading reviewer with one that runs its own concurrent probe on a real race, and test a rubric policy that punishes a correct simple task.
objectives: Explain why builder flags are not evidence.
Run an independent probe.
Know what a probe cannot prove.
Check whether a task has material assumptions.
Keep the human approval step.
objectivesKn: builder flags ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯವಲ್ಲ ಏಕೆ ಎಂದು ವಿವರಿಸಿ.

    def __init__(self, safe=False):
        self.charges = []
        self.seen = set()
        self.lock = threading.Lock() if safe else None

    def _charge(self, key):
        if key not in self.seen:
            time.sleep(0.05)
            self.seen.add(key)
            self.charges.append(key)

    def pay(self, key):
        if self.lock:
            with self.lock:
                self._charge(key)
        else:
            self._charge(key)


def sequential_test(cls):
    p = cls()
    p.pay("k1"); p.pay("k1")
    return len(p.charges) == 1


def concurrent_probe(cls, workers=4):
    p = cls()
    ts = [threading.Thread(target=p.pay, args=("k1",)) for _ in range(workers)]
    for t in ts:
        t.start()
    for t in ts:
        t.join()
    return len(p.charges)


class Safe(Payments):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(safe=True)


def problem_fit_from_flags(state):
    return 2 if state.get("solves_requested_problem") else 0


def problem_fit_from_probe(cls):
    return 2 if concurrent_probe(cls) == 1 else 0


def assumptions_score(assumptions, material):
    return 0 if not assumptions else 2


def assumptions_score_fixed(assumptions, material):
    if not material:

One reviewer reads the builder flag; the other scores from the probe.","descKn":"Payments ಕೀಲಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ ಎರಡು ಹಂತಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ವಿಳಂಬದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, lock ಅದನ್ನು ಮುಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. sequential_test pay ಅನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಬಾರಿ ಕರೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. concurrent_probe ಒಂದೇ ಕೀಲಿಗೆ ಹಲವು threads ಆರಂಭಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು reviewer builder flag ಓದುತ್ತದೆ; ಇನ್ನೊಂದು probe ಯಿಂದ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"class Payments:
    def __init__(self, safe=False):
        self.charges = []
        self.seen = set()
        self.lock = threading.Lock() if safe else None

    def _charge(self, key):
        if key not in self.seen:
            time.sleep(0.05)
            self.seen.add(key)
            self.charges.append(key)

    def pay(self, key):
        if self.lock:
            with self.lock:
                self._charge(key)
        else:
            self._charge(key)


def sequential_test(cls):
    p = cls()
    p.pay("k1"); p.pay("k1")
    return len(p.charges) == 1


def concurrent_probe(cls, workers=4):
    p = cls()
    ts = [threading.Thread(target=p.pay, args=("k1",)) for _ in range(workers)]
    for t in ts:
        t.start()
    for t in ts:
        t.join()
    return len(p.charges)


class Safe(Payments):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(safe=True)


def problem_fit_from_flags(state):
    return 2 if state.get("solves_requested_problem") else 0


def problem_fit_from_probe(cls):
    return 2 if concurrent_probe(cls) == 1 else 0


def assumptions_score(assumptions, material):
    return 0 if not assumptions else 2


def assumptions_score_fixed(assumptions, material):
    if not material:
        return 2
    return 2 if assumptions else 0"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"rv_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() runs the sequential test on both versions, probes both with four threads, compares the two reviewers, repeats the two-thread probe five times and tests two assumption policies.","descKn":"main() ಎರಡೂ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಅನುಕ್ರಮ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಓಡಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು threads ನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಎರಡನ್ನೂ probe ಮಾಡಿ, ಎರಡು reviewers ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು-thread probe ಐದು ಬಾರಿ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಎರಡು ಊಹೆ ನೀತಿಗಳನ್ನು ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the sequential test passes and hides the defect")
    print("sequential test, unsafe implementation:", sequential_test(Payments))
    print("sequential test, locked implementation:", sequential_test(Safe))
    print("both versions pass the only test the builder wrote, so a verification gate that ran it would report success for the unsafe one; the test never asked the question the task was about")

    section("2. Genuinely running: a concurrent probe on the same two implementations")
    for name, cls in (("unsafe", Payments), ("locked", Safe)):
        print(f"{name:7} charges created by 4 simultaneous requests with one key: {concurrent_probe(cls)}")
    print("the unsafe version charged the same key several times because the check and the insert are separate steps with a delay between them (the delay was added to force the overlap, so the number of duplicates is an artefact of the lab), and the locked version charged once")

    section("3. Genuinely comparing: a reviewer that reads flags versus one that runs the probe")
    builder_state = {"solves_requested_problem": True}
    print("builder reports it solved the problem; the unsafe code was submitted")
    print("flag-reading reviewer problem_fit    :", problem_fit_from_flags(builder_state))
    print("probe-running reviewer problem_fit   :", problem_fit_from_probe(Payments))
    print("probe-running reviewer on locked code:", problem_fit_from_probe(Safe))
    print("the flag-reading reviewer gave full marks because it read the builder's own claim, which is the failure the separation of builder and marker is meant to prevent; the reviewer that ran an independent probe scored the same code 0, and a reviewer is only independent if its evidence is")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: the probe is a sample, not a proof")
    counts = [concurrent_probe(Payments, workers=2) for _ in range(5)]
    print("duplicates seen over 5 runs with 2 workers on the unsafe code:", counts)
    print("with the delay forced into the code, every run exposed the race; this lab did not measure a race without the forced delay, but a probe can only show that an overlap happened in the runs tried, so a failing probe demonstrates a defect and a passing probe does not demonstrate its absence, which is one reason the human approval step remains")

    section("5. Genuinely checking: a rubric policy that punishes a correct simple task")
    print("simple task, no material assumptions, none listed -> lesson policy:", assumptions_score((), material=False), "| refined policy:", assumptions_score_fixed((), material=False))
    print("payment task with a material assumption, none listed -> lesson policy:", assumptions_score((), material=True), "| refined policy:", assumptions_score_fixed((), material=True))
    print("the simple rule 'empty assumptions scores 0' hard-fails a correct one-line change because a zero forces hard_fail; asking whether the task has material assumptions first avoids that, and still scores a payment task with unstated assumptions 0")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


def snapshot(inp):
    return Inputs(inp.task, copy.deepcopy(inp.state))


def nosy_reviewer(inp):
    inp.state["solves_requested_problem"] = True
    return "reviewed"


def verdict(total, minimum, pass_at, soft_at):
    if minimum == 0 or total < soft_at:
        return "hard_fail"
    return "soft_fail" if total < pass_at else "pass"


RUBRIC = {"1.0": {"pass_at": 7, "soft_at": 5}, "1.1": {"pass_at": 8, "soft_at": 6}}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"rv_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() tries assignment and dict mutation on a frozen object, runs a nosy reviewer on the original and on a copy, hashes a file at start and end of a review, applies two rubric versions to four score patterns and writes a report.","descKn":"main() frozen ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ನಿಯೋಜನೆ ಮತ್ತು dict ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, ಕುತೂಹಲಿ reviewer ಅನ್ನು ಮೂಲ ಮತ್ತು ನಕಲಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ಓಡಿಸಿ, review ಆರಂಭ ಮತ್ತು ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಫೈಲ್ hash ಮಾಡಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅಂಕ ಮಾದರಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಎರಡು rubric ಆವೃತ್ತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸಿ ವರದಿ ಬರೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely checking: what 'frozen' protects")
    inp = Inputs("task", {"solves_requested_problem": False})
    try:
        inp.task = "other"
        print("assigning a field: allowed")
    except FrozenInstanceError:
        print("assigning a field: FrozenInstanceError")
    try:
        inp.state = {}
    except FrozenInstanceError:
        print("replacing the state dict: FrozenInstanceError")
    inp.state["solves_requested_problem"] = True
    print("mutating the dict inside the frozen object: allowed, state is now", inp.state)
    print("a frozen dataclass stops attribute assignment and not changes to the dict it holds, so a reviewer given such an object can still rewrite the evidence it is judging")

    section("2. Genuinely running: a reviewer that edits what it reviews")
    original = Inputs("task", {"solves_requested_problem": False})
    before = digest(original.state)
    nosy_reviewer(original)
    print("evidence hash before:", before, "| after the review:", digest(original.state), "| changed:", before != digest(original.state))
    given = Inputs("task", {"solves_requested_problem": False})
    snap = snapshot(given)
    nosy_reviewer(snap)
    print("same reviewer on a deep copy: original hash unchanged:", digest(given.state) == before)
    print("the edit reached the builder's evidence when the reviewer was handed the original and stayed in the copy otherwise; a prompt telling the reviewer not to edit files is not a boundary, an isolated copy with a recorded hash is")

    section("3. Genuinely running: a file-based evidence bundle and a tamper check")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        ev = Path(d) / "feedback.json"
        ev.write_text(json.dumps({"tests_match_requirement": False}), encoding="utf-8")
        h = hashlib.sha256(ev.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]
        print("hash recorded when the review starts:", h)
        ev.write_text(json.dumps({"tests_match_requirement": True}), encoding="utf-8")
        h2 = hashlib.sha256(ev.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]
        print("hash when the review ends:", h2, "| evidence changed during the review:", h != h2)
    print("recording the hash at the start and comparing at the end detects a change but cannot say who made it or prevent it; preventing it needs permissions the reviewer does not have, which a local script cannot supply")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: the same scores under two rubric versions")
    cases = {"7 with no zero": (7, 1), "6 with no zero": (6, 1), "5 with no zero": (5, 1), "9 with a zero": (9, 0)}
    for name, (total, mn) in cases.items():
        print(f"{name:16}", {v: verdict(total, mn, **p) for v, p in RUBRIC.items()})
    print("the same scores were pass under version 1.0 and soft_fail under 1.1 for a total of 7, and a total of 5 moved from soft_fail to hard_fail; a report without a rubric version cannot be compared with one from before the change, and the zero rule gave hard_fail in both")

    section("5. Genuinely running: a report with traceability fields")
    evidence = {"task": "task", "state": {"solves_requested_problem": False}}
    report = {"rubric_version": "1.1", "reviewer_version": "stub-1", "input_hash": digest(evidence), "total": 7, "verdict": verdict(7, 1, **RUBRIC["1.1"])}
    text = json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    print(text)
    print("the same evidence hashes to the same value on every run:", digest(evidence) == digest(copy.deepcopy(evidence)), "| a changed field changes it:", digest(dict(evidence, task="x")) != digest(evidence))
    print("the version fields and input hash let a later session tell whether two reviews used the same rubric and the same evidence; the reviewer version here is a label we made up")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


def snapshot(inp):
    return Inputs(inp.task, copy.deepcopy(inp.state))


def nosy_reviewer(inp):
    inp.state["solves_requested_problem"] = True
    return "reviewed"


def verdict(total, minimum, pass_at, soft_at):
    if minimum == 0 or total < soft_at:
        return "hard_fail"
    return "soft_fail" if total < pass_at else "pass"
